clue.text: Concoction full of Argentinian fruit

indicators.note: a thing full of something holds it inside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a concoction can be a made-up story, a falsehood
Che Guevara, the Argentinian-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: Someone describes a drink mixed up from South American fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Che Guevara, the revolutionary, was born in Argentina, which is why he stands for the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: The lichee, more often spelt lychee, is a small sweet Chinese fruit with a rough red skin.

clue.text: Anne plays with a lot of babies

indicators.note: playing about with something means moving its parts round freely, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Anne amuses herself by playing with a crowd of infants.
explanation.definitionFit: Neonatal is the adjective for newborn infants, so it works as the phrase describing things concerning them.

clue.text: Irish republican breaking law over in Merseyside location

indicators.note: something breaking another piece splits it open and sits in the gap
in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round
IR is a standard abbreviation for Irish
R abbreviates Republican

explanation.surface: An Irish rebel breaks the law somewhere on Merseyside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wirral is a peninsula in Merseyside, the county around Liverpool in north-west England.

clue.text: Anita oddly cuddles rotter in Canadian region

indicators.note: to cuddle someone is to wrap your arms round them, so one piece holds the other
oddly points to the letters in the odd-numbered positions, first, third and fifth

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of the name
a cad is a dishonourable man, an old-fashioned rotter

explanation.surface: Anita, behaving strangely, embraces a scoundrel somewhere in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' reads as 'strangely' in the surface; here it picks letters by position.
explanation.definitionFit: Acadia was the old French colony in eastern Canada, roughly today's Maritime provinces, and the name survives for that area.

clue.text: End the call for inhibition

definitions.meaning: first meaning: put the telephone down
second meaning: a psychological block or neurosis

explanation.surface: A therapist suggests ending phone calls as a cure for shyness.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb is two words, hang up; the noun takes a hyphen.
explanation.definitionFit: As a phrasal verb it means finishing a phone conversation; as a noun a hang-up is an emotional problem holding someone back.

clue.text: American with ale gut developed fundamental muscle?

indicators.note: something developed has grown into a new form, so the letters take a new shape

parts.note: US abbreviates American
taken as written

explanation.surface: A beer-bellied American builds up an essential muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: The fundament is the buttocks, so 'fundamental' here means belonging to the bottom, not basic; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The glutaeus, usually spelt gluteus, is any of the large muscles forming the buttock.

clue.text: Square creep catches group of 19

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three
to inch is to creep forward slowly
to nail a criminal is to catch them

explanation.surface: An unpopular, sneaky person gets caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square creep' reads as an insult for a dull sneak; each word is in fact a separate verb or number. The 19 points to the clue answered by the band's frontman.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine Inch Nails is the American industrial rock band led by Trent Reznor, the answer at 19.

clue.text: See 7
See 7
Drink for the French lieutenant — bottles of Irish wine

parts.note: the drink is slang for the sea, and the French word for sea is mer

indicators.note: to bottle something is to shut it up inside, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: LT abbreviates lieutenant
O' in Irish surnames such as O'Brien means 'descendant of'

explanation.surface: An officer drinks French wine while keeping hold of some Irish wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is old slang for the sea; O goes inside LT.
explanation.definitionFit: Merlot is a red grape variety and the wine made from it, grown widely in Bordeaux.

clue.text: British unit did get 26 endlessly when at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are mixed up
without its end, the final letter of the word is lost

parts.note: taken as written
the answer to clue 26, cut short
taken as written

explanation.surface: A British sailor complains of getting injured at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: HURT loses its T before all the letters are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: The hundredweight is an imperial measure of weight, 112 pounds in Britain, and twenty of them make a ton.

clue.text: Naughty pair I let in zoology class

indicators.note: naughty children will not behave or stay in line, so the letters are out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher admits to letting a badly behaved pair into a biology lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class' looks like a schoolroom, but it is the biological rank above order.
explanation.definitionFit: Reptilia is the taxonomic class containing snakes, lizards, turtles and crocodiles.

clue.text: Cover up topless swimmer

indicators.note: without a top, the first letter of the word is cut off, the top in a down entry

parts.note: to hide something is to cover it up

explanation.surface: A bather without a bikini top is told to cover herself.
explanation.walkthrough: HIDE loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The ide is a European freshwater fish of the carp family, a staple crossword fish.

clue.text: After drinks journalist tripped

parts.note: an animal laps when it drinks with its tongue
ED is the editor, the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter stumbled after a few drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To lapse is to slip or fall into error, so lapsed is a past-tense match for having slipped up.

clue.text: French composer takes part in formal discussions

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so the composer's name encloses the other piece

parts.note: Léo Delibes, composer of the ballet Coppélia
a ration is a share or allotted part

explanation.surface: A French composer joins in formal talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes part in' looks like one phrase, but 'takes' is the container signal and 'part' a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberations are careful considered debates, typically of a jury or committee.

clue.text: Delivered baby's family needs — material for garments

indicators.note: a speech is delivered out loud, so what follows is judged by its sound

parts.note: baby and dear are both terms of endearment
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: A newborn's relatives need clothing material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivered baby' paints a birth, but 'Delivered' signals speech; only the first part is sounded.
explanation.definitionFit: Deerskin is leather from a deer's hide, used for gloves, jackets and moccasins.

clue.text: He composed Sweeney Todd?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the American composer Samuel, known for his Adagio for Strings
second meaning: the trade of the Demon of Fleet Street, a hairdresser

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as if someone wrote the music for Sweeney Todd, which was Sondheim; the man and the character are separate.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Barber was an American composer, and Sweeney Todd is the fictional murderous barber of Fleet Street.

clue.text: One flighty brute, not sick of Proust

indicators.note: not means without, so the following piece is taken away

parts.note: a brute is a beast
mal is French for ill, and Proust wrote in French

explanation.surface: A fickle thug, never tired of reading Proust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sick of' looks like weary of, but it means sick in Proust's language.
explanation.definitionFit: The ani is a black tropical American bird of the cuckoo family, so it is one creature able to take flight.

clue.text: Instruments needed for getting into car in Asia

indicators.note: the letters needed are contained within the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word to the start of the last

explanation.surface: Someone asks which tools are required to break into a car in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocarinas are small egg-shaped wind instruments with finger holes, often made of clay.

clue.text: Ezra Norton loses 20 11 on River Trent?

indicators.note: a name that loses something has those letters taken away from it

parts.note: R abbreviates river
the name taken as written
twenty hundredweight, the answer at 11, make a ton

explanation.surface: A man named Ezra Norton loses a lot of weight living beside an English river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fifteensquared parse puts R on the front of EZ (Ezra, as the Bible book is abbreviated) and NOR(TON) with its TON lost. 'River Trent' looks like the Midlands river; the definition is a first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Trent Reznor is the American musician who founded and fronts Nine Inch Nails, so Trent is a given name pointing to this surname.

clue.text: The years of immaturity, say, soon will be over

indicators.note: turned over, in a down entry, means flipped so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: eg, for example, is what 'say' means in 'pick a number, say five'
anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: Someone reassures a teenager that their awkward years will soon be over.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonage is the period of legal minority, before coming of age, and by extension any time of immaturity.

clue.text: German chancellor presents small business model in speech

indicators.note: in speech means as spoken, so the pieces are judged by their sound

parts.note: biz is a short informal word for business
a marque is a make or model of car

explanation.surface: A German leader unveils a template for a small firm in an address.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto von Bismarck was the first Chancellor of the German Empire, unifying the country in 1871.

clue.text: Intensely study book to get ahead of others

parts.note: B abbreviates book
to be one up is to have an advantage over rivals

explanation.surface: A student studies hard with a textbook to beat their classmates.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a single piece of exam advice; the definition is the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To bone up is an informal idiom for cramming, studying a subject hard before a test.

clue.text: Beds used by active working girls when retiring

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the combined pieces are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: A abbreviates active, as in grammar
working girls is a euphemism for prostitutes

explanation.surface: Beds are used by busy prostitutes when they go to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beds' and 'retiring' suggest bedtime; here beds are layers of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are layers of sedimentary rock, which geologists also call beds.

clue.text: Not so far from Cork?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a thing that shuts, like a stopper in a bottle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cork' looks like the Irish city, inviting a place nearby; the question mark marks it as a bottle stopper.
explanation.definitionFit: Closer is the comparative of close, meaning nearer, and as a noun it is anything that closes something, such as a cork.

clue.text: Barons unhappy with a dinner in US city

indicators.note: unhappy suggests things are out of sorts and disturbed, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Aristocrats are displeased with a meal in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: San Bernardino is a city in southern California, east of Los Angeles.

clue.text: Greedy sort of bank in Paraguay hacked by current German government

indicators.note: something hacked into is broken open with other material inside it

parts.note: PY is Paraguay's international vehicle code
I is the symbol for electric current
G abbreviates German
G abbreviates government

explanation.surface: A greedy bank in Paraguay is attacked by computer hackers from the German regime.
explanation.walkthrough: Both definitions come before the wordplay: one adjective, and one word that completes a common phrase for a money box.
explanation.definitionFit: Piggy is a childish adjective for gluttonous, and a piggy bank is a pig-shaped money box.

clue.text: Actor once a day gets tense in the back

indicators.note: in the back places the next piece at the rear of what remains

parts.note: THUR abbreviates Thursday
T abbreviates tense, in grammar

explanation.surface: A former actor tenses up in his back over the course of a day.
explanation.walkthrough: The T of THUR moves to the end. 'Once' marks the actor as no longer living.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Hurt was an English actor, known for The Elephant Man and Alien, who died in 2017.

clue.text: One of the Eloi after losing heart comes back again

indicators.note: coming back means returning, so the letters run the other way
the heart is the centre, so the middle letter of the name goes

parts.note: Weena is the Eloi girl in H G Wells's The Time Machine

explanation.surface: A dispirited Eloi from The Time Machine returns once more.
explanation.walkthrough: Weena loses her middle E and is turned round. The Eloi are the gentle surface people of the far future in Wells's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Anew means afresh, once more, which is a straight synonym for again.
